title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a stray sheet of general category theory. It is unrelated to the preceding page, which computes H^1(Q,T)' for the CM torus T. Its content is the material that became SGA 3 Exp. IV §1 (Demazure) and SGA 4 Exp. I (Grothendieck–Verdier), on epimorphic families, sieves and generators.

(1) Variants of epimorphicity. For a family (u_i: X_i -> X) in a category C there are five variants: epimorphic, strict epimorphic, effective epimorphic, universally effective and universally strict. If fibre products exist in C, 'strict' and 'effective' coincide, so only four variants remain. All of them depend only on the sieve R that the family generates.

(2) Prop. 0. The notions 'epimorphic' and 'strictly epimorphic', and likewise the three other variants, are stable under enlarging the family, i.e. under passing to a larger sieve.

(3) Setting. Let G be a set of objects of C and \underline{G} the full subcategory it spans.

(4) Prop. 1. The following are equivalent.
(a) For every X, the family of all arrows G_i -> X with G_i in G is epimorphic (resp. strictly epimorphic). In modern terms: G is a generating (resp. strict generating) family.
(b) For every X, consider the comma category \underline{G}/X -> C and the canonical cocone colim_{T in \underline{G}/X} T -> X, read representably. The natural map Hom(X,Y) -> lim_{(T->X)} Hom(T,Y), natural in Y, is a mono (resp. an iso).
In the 'resp.' case, (b) says that \underline{G} is a dense subcategory: every object is canonically a colimit of objects of G.

(5) Proof. The non-'resp.' case is tautological. For the 'resp.' case, the proof starts unpacking (a): for every Y, (i) h_Y(X) -> \prod h_Y(G_i) is injective, and (ii) compatible families f_i glue. The page breaks off here, and the next page is crossed out and illegible.
errors: Prop. 0 as transcribed claims that 'strictly epimorphic' (not only the universal variants) is stable under enlarging the family/sieve. For R ⊂ R' with R strict, h_Y(X) -> Hom(R',h_Y) is injective. Surjectivity, however, requires that an element of Hom(R',h_Y) be determined by its restriction to R. That holds if, for each f: T->X in R', the pulled-back sieve f^*R is epimorphic on T, which is automatic only in the universal variants. Whether the plain strict case holds in full generality is doubtful (I am unsure); the reading of the line is also uncertain.

In Prop. 1, the gap between (a) and (b) in the strict case is that compatibility in (a) is tested against arbitrary T in C, whereas in (b) it is tested only along morphisms of \underline{G}/X. The gap is bridged by applying the epimorphicity of (a) to the test object T itself. The proof on the page is incomplete (cut off), but the statement is correct.

ideas.what: Five variants of epimorphic families (epi, strict, effective, universally strict, universally effective); strict = effective when fibre products exist; dependence only on the generated sieve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; Demazure (SGA 3 Exp. IV), Grothendieck–Verdier (SGA 4 Exp. I)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 Exp. IV §1; SGA 4 Exp. I §10

ideas.what: Stability of epimorphic-type sieves under enlargement
A family G is a (strict) generating family iff every X is (canonically) the colimit over \underline{G}/X, i.e. \underline{G} is dense
ideas.modern_name: strict generator = dense subcategory (canonical colimit / density theorem)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. I (generating families, strict generators)

deep.surprise_reason: These are draft notes of standard material later published in SGA 3 Exp. IV and SGA 4 Exp. I. They are of interest only as evidence of drafting in the 1964–65 period.
transcription_corrections: 'cet système est' should read 'ce système est'.
Struck words: 'cinq' (in Prop. 0, replaced by the list of notions) and 'strict' (before '(resp. isomorphique)' in b)).

The end of the Prop. 0 line ('n'en dépendent que des épimorphismes quarrables') is doubtful. It plausibly says that the notions depend only on the sieve generated, or involves 'quarrables'; the image is ambiguous.
Line 6 most likely reads 'sur le crible R engendré'. The parenthetical after it is illegible.
